newsitem.title: USA: First Merchants named in another lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: First Merchants named in another lawsuit.

text.p: First Merchants Acceptance has been named in another class-action lawsuit, filed Wednesday in U.S. District Court in Chicago, lawyers for the plaintiffs said.

The action, filed by the law firm Abbey, Gardy & Squitieri LLP, alleges the sub-prime lender's directors and officers misrepresented and concealed material facts concerning the company's financial results, the attorneys said.
The complaint also alleges First Merchants withheld information that its financial books contained unauthorized entries overstating its fiscal 1996 results.

On April 16, the company said it discovered irregularities in its 1996 records. On May 15, it said it estimated its 1996 net earnings would be restated to between $0.50 and $0.70 per share versus the $1.56 per share originally reported.
The company also said in May it would issue its restated results by the end of June.
In the weeks following the April announcement, several class-action suits were filed in federal court in Illinois on behalf of shareholders.
The suit filed Wednesday is on behalf of buyers of First Merchants stock between January 25, 1996, and April 16, 1997.
Stephen Fearon, an attorney with the law firm, said he expected the suit filed Wednesday to be consolidated with the previous actions filed against First Merchants.
Based in Deerfield, Ill., First Merchants makes automobile loans to individuals with poor or no credit, a market sector referred to as sub-prime.
